name: Roys Peak Track
why: Two hours of zigzags straight up a sheep farm, then the ridge everyone photographs: Lake Wānaka's arms below and the Southern Alps behind.
book: Free, no permit. Closed for lambing 1 October to 10 November. The car park, 6 km west of Wānaka on the Mount Aspiring Road, fills early: walk or cycle out on the Waterfall Creek and Glendhu Bay tracks, or take a shuttle.
water: None on the track and no shade: carry 2-3 litres in summer.
dangers: Steep and exposed the whole way: in summer heat and sun are the problem, in winter snow and ice.
Wind and cold on the summit ridge even on warm days: carry a warm layer and a shell.
The track crosses private farmland: stay on it, gates as you find them.
turnaround: Not at the photo viewpoint by 13:00: take your picture there and go back down.

points.name: Roys Peak car park
points.note: On the Mount Aspiring Road by the lake; the track climbs straight from the gate through farmland.

points.name: Roys Peak ridge viewpoint
points.note: The famous photo spot on the ridge, about 30 minutes below the summit, with the lake's arms on both sides.

points.name: Roys Peak summit
points.note: 1,578 m: Mount Aspiring to the west, Lake Wānaka and the Clutha basin to the east. Return the same way.
